name: Amma
role: Creator god and source of order in Dogon accounts
fun_fact: In the Griaule-Dieterlen account Amma shaped the world from an egg, though Dogon ideas about the creator vary and that synthesis is contested.

name: Nommo
role: Ancestral twin beings who mediate between sky and earth
fun_fact: The Nommo are usually described as twins, and in the published account they descend in an ark bringing water and speech.

name: Ogo
role: The pale fox, a first being who brings disorder
fun_fact: Ogo is called the pale fox, and in Dogon fox divination his footprints are read as signs.

name: Faro
role: Water spirit and lawgiver honoured across Mande and Dogon traditions
fun_fact: Faro is associated with water and speech, and some accounts make him one of the Nommo while others give him a separate role.

name: Sunjata
role: Hero of the Mande epic and traditional founder of the Mali Empire
fun_fact: In the epic Sunjata learns to walk with an iron rod and then uproots a baobab tree to prove his strength.

name: Sogolon
role: Sunjata's mother, remembered as the buffalo woman
fun_fact: Sogolon is called the buffalo woman because of the buffalo heritage attributed to her in the epic, and her difficult pregnancy marks her son's destiny.

name: Soumaoro Kanté
role: King of Sosso and Sunjata's great rival
fun_fact: In many tellings Soumaoro can be wounded only by a white rooster's spur, a secret that Balla Fasséké helps to uncover.

name: Balla Fasséké
role: Sunjata's griot, musician and keeper of memory
fun_fact: Balla Fasséké is remembered as the first griot of the Keita court, and his heirs are said to keep the Sunjata epic.

name: Sassouma Bérété
role: Sunjata's stepmother and rival at court
fun_fact: Sassouma Bérété mocks Sogolon and her son who cannot walk, and her ambition for her own child drives Sunjata's family toward exile.

name: Fakoli
role: Soumaoro's nephew and a formidable warrior
fun_fact: Fakoli turns against his uncle after a deep humiliation, and his defection becomes one of the turning points of the war.
